clue.text: Get by policeman, last in line

parts.note: a cop is an informal word for a policeman

indicators.note: last in signals that only the final letter of the word line is taken

explanation.surface: An officer gets by while waiting at the back of a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to manage or cope with a situation, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Tripe — cold piece friend served up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: served up in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a piece
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A cold slice of offal handed to a friend at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses PART and PAL to give LAPTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, besides offal, is slang for nonsense, which is a synonym of empty talk.

clue.text: Steel structure only demolished under pressure

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the rearranged letters below the other piece

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: demolished suggests the letters of only are knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A steel framework is torn down only because of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice tower carrying power lines, a type of steel structure.

clue.text: Speak in clubs about poetry

parts.note: C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
verse is another word for poetry

explanation.surface: Someone recites poems in nightclubs or golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk or speak with someone, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Severe test of French in examination

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A tough French test during an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience, a severe test of endurance.

clue.text: Misfortune during holiday leads to indecision

indicators.note: during says one piece occurs in the middle of the other

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday
ill means misfortune, as in ills befalling someone

explanation.surface: Bad luck on a trip leaves someone unable to decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacillation is wavering between choices, the state of indecision.

clue.text: Revolutionary American university in revolutionary broadcast

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: red is a byword for a revolutionary, a communist

indicators.note: Revolutionary here signals turning round the name of the university

parts.note: Yale is an American university

explanation.surface: A radical American college transmitted on revolutionary radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word appears twice with two jobs: the capitalised one signals a turnaround, the lower-case one is red, a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Relayed means passed on or transmitted, as a broadcast is.

clue.text: Greek character describing northern volcano

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing around, puts one piece around the other

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person describing a volcano in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, an example of a volcano.

clue.text: Granted, everyone had debts

parts.note: all means everyone
someone who had debts owed money

explanation.surface: An admission that every single person was in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something granted is permitted, a synonym in the sense of a request being given approval.

clue.text: How heavy, tau, when broken down — and similar things

indicators.note: when broken down suggests the letters of how heavy, tau are split up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about the weight of a Greek letter once dismantled.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase completes 'and ...', so the dash and 'and' join the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tacked onto a list means other things of the same kind, much like et cetera.

clue.text: Body part discovered in Pimlico, London

indicators.note: discovered in says the letters are found lying inside the words Pimlico, London

explanation.surface: A grisly find of a human remain in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimlico is a district of central London; the answer spans the end of one place name and the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the large intestine, an organ and so an example of a body part.

clue.text: Popular music centre of plainly neat construction

indicators.note: construction suggests the letters of plainly neat are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A description of a music venue built in a plain, tidy style.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin Pan Alley was the street in New York, and later Denmark Street in London, where popular song publishers clustered.
explanation.definitionFit: The name became shorthand for the popular music publishing industry, so it is a centre of that music.

clue.text: Popular flavour available

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
to season is to add flavour

explanation.surface: A favourite taste is now on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce that is in season is readily available at that time of year.

clue.text: Burning land

definitions.meaning: on fire, as a candle that is lit
to come down and settle, as a bird or a passenger getting off a bus

explanation.surface: Two words with no picture: a fire and an arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both on fire and to descend from a vehicle or settle, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: In charge, one head showing hostility

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A single boss showing aggression to the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is coldness of manner, an unfriendly frostiness close to hostility.

clue.text: Such a plot may bring danger

indicators.note: may bring suggests the letters of danger, rearranged, can produce the plot in question

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain scheme or plan could be hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme, but here it is a piece of ground; the anagram of DANGER gives that ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot of land, so it is an example of such a plot.

clue.text: Guide English class absorbing chapter

indicators.note: absorbing says one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: A tour leader for an English lesson that takes in a chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany and guide them, a synonym.

clue.text: Make inquiries about it, seeing a TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests the letters of it seeing a TV are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a story after watching a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate something is to examine it closely, which is making inquiries about it.

clue.text: Superior, British in flying boat

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
flying suggests the letters of boat are sent all over the place

explanation.surface: Someone of higher standing, a Briton aboard a seaplane.
explanation.walkthrough: A flying boat is a seaplane, but 'flying' is the anagram signal on BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey, a religious superior in that crossword-favoured sense.

clue.text: Word: also sentence

definitions.meaning: a word or expression, especially a technical one

explanation.surface: A grammar note that a word may also be a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a name for something and a length of time served in prison.

clue.text: Opposing troops some cavalrymen eventually pushed back

indicators.note: pushed back says the selected letters are read in the opposite direction
some says only part of the words cavalrymen eventually is used

explanation.surface: Mounted soldiers finally driven into retreat by an advancing force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks YMENE from the end of cavalrymen and the start of eventually; 'pushed back' turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the hostile force on the other side, the troops opposing yours.

clue.text: Several books in one vehicle

definitions.meaning: a single volume collecting several works
a bus, an old name for a public road vehicle

explanation.surface: A traveller reading several books while riding in one vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a collected edition of several works and the old full name of a bus.

clue.text: Fly with squadron leader, stop coming in low

indicators.note: coming in says the following pieces are placed inside another

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: leader signals the first letter of the word squadron

parts.note: quit means stop

explanation.surface: An air force officer flies with a squadron and halts, approaching at low altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' suggests height, but it is the call of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is a small biting insect, a kind of fly; it was also a wartime aircraft.

clue.text: Shock caused by unusual feat? No end

indicators.note: No end says the final letter is dropped from the word for the feat

parts.note: a stunt is a daring or unusual feat

explanation.surface: Amazement caused by a remarkable, unending achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' removes the T from STUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or astonish them, a synonym.
